title: Artifact Sharing Audit
summary: Checks how each page tied to Swami's skills is shared against who should see it, rescans his skills for problems, and refreshes his private Skill Maintenance dashboard with both.
what_it_is: A housekeeping skill for Swami's own skills. Many of his skills publish pages on claude.ai: skill-sheet drafts, the Skill Library, tools and dashboards. Some of those should be open to anyone with the link and some should stay private. This skill reads how each one is shared right now, compares it with how it should be shared, and tells Swami which ones to change.

In the same run it scans every one of his skills for known kinds of staleness and conflict (old tool names, old save locations, missing skills, stray files, out-of-date skill sheets and more), and rebuilds the private **Skill Maintenance** dashboard that shows both results. Claude cannot change sharing; it only reads it. Swami changes it himself from each page's **Share** menu.
why: Owner-only hiding is not privacy: anything hidden on a page is still in its source, so a page shared by link can leak what it hides. A draft shared by link would also go live the moment it is edited, before Swami vets it. A regular audit catches both.

what_it_does.text: Reads the sharing state of every page tied to the skills (Private, Public or Invited) with a fresh read of each page, never from a title or an old result.

Applies one rule: a page may be public only when everyone who could open it could see that content anyway **and** nothing in its source is private. Pages fall into three groups: Public, Private, and Case by case.
Adds any new skill-related page from the artifact listing (titles ending in "skill", the Skill Library, pages a skill builds) to `sharing.json`, with what it should be and why.
Records every change in sharing state, and every page added or retired, in a dated history (Eastern Time).

Runs `scan.py` over all of Swami's skills: old tool names, old save locations, dashboard steps older than vibe-dashboard, missing skills, stray cache files, no version line, very large SKILL.md files, acronym rule conflicts, missing or out-of-date skill sheets, Fusion add-in rule conflicts and differing Comet support. Each finding is rated High, Medium or Low.
Keeps a hand-kept list (`known.json`) of problems the scan cannot find, and closes them once Swami has fixed them.

Rebuilds the private Skill Maintenance dashboard with `build.py` in the vibe-dashboard design system (Search, Mind Map, Glossary and a spoken audio overview), then republishes it to the same link, still private.
Replies in chat with a table of mismatches only (Title, Shared now, Should be, What to do; NDA pages first), the counts, the scan summary, and how to change sharing.
Gives the dashboard an owner-only **Update now** button that starts the same run as an on-demand scheduled task, with a choice of Haiku or Sonnet for the page checks.
On request, checks every artifact on the account, not just the skill pages. That report stays in chat and never goes on the dashboard.

triggers: Or click **Update now** on the Skill Maintenance dashboard

how_to_use.step: In a Claude chat on the Mac (desktop app or web), say "check skill sharing" or "refresh skill maintenance". Or open the Skill Maintenance dashboard and click **Update now** in the Sharing Status section, pick Haiku or Sonnet, then **Start update**.
Reads Swami's memory for people under NDA and keeps them in a private working file for the privacy scan. They are never written to the dashboard or its files.
Reads the dashboard's published `sharing.json`, `known.json` and `narration.txt`, then lists the account's artifacts and adds any new skill-related page.
Reads each page's sharing state in small helper agents (about 5 pages each, on Haiku by default) and updates `sharing.json` with the time checked and any changes.
Runs `scan.py` over every skill, with the public skill-sheet registry from GitHub, and reviews the findings.
Runs `build.py`, updates and records the audio narration, runs the privacy scan, checks the page in a headless browser, and republishes the dashboard privately.
Posts the mismatch table and counts in chat (a button run notifies the phone only if a page needs changing or the run fails).
For each mismatch: open the page in the browser, click **Share**, and choose Private or invite people by email. Then ask for a re-check.

how_to_use_windows.step: Same as on the Mac: in the Claude desktop app or claude.ai in Edge or Chrome, say "check skill sharing", or click **Update now** on the dashboard. Nothing runs on the PC itself.
Identical to macOS steps 2 to 7: everything runs in Claude's workspace and on claude.ai.
Open each page in Edge or Chrome, click **Share**, and pick Private or invite people by email.

capabilities.text: Sharing state comes only from a fresh read of each page, so the report is never a guess.
Page reads run in parallel helper agents on Haiku, which keeps token use low; Sonnet is one click away when Haiku can't read a page.
Every scan check is mechanical (text and file patterns), so two runs on the same skills give the same findings.
The Update now button reruns the whole audit unattended in about 5 to 10 minutes and only notifies the phone when something needs Swami.
A privacy scan of the page, its data files and its narration runs before every publish.

limitations.text: Claude cannot change sharing. Swami changes each page from its **Share** menu.
The artifact listing returns at most 200 pages and is a lower bound; older pages beyond it can be missed.
By default only pages tied to the skills are checked. A full audit of every artifact has to be asked for.
Claude never changes what a page should be except for a new page; that is Swami's call, especially for the Case by case group.
A page that can't be read is marked "couldn't read" and keeps its last known state.

gotchas.text: Owner-only rows, cards and columns are not privacy: they are still in the page source. A page with owner-only parts follows the rule like any other.
A skill-sheet draft shared by link is harmless only while it matches its GitHub Pages copy; the next edit would go live before Swami vets it. Keep drafts private.
Recording the audio leaves a `__pycache__` folder in the vibe-dashboard skill copy. Delete it (and run Python with `-B`) or the next scan reports stray files.
Only a read **without** a path reports sharing state. Reading a published file such as `index.html` does not.
Republish the dashboard without a `capabilities` field so it keeps its permission for the Update now button; passing an empty one removes it.
A page Swami set to Private after being told to is recorded in the history as done on the next check, not before.
If the Skill Maintenance update task is deleted or renamed, update `TRIGGER` in `build.py` and the task id in the skill, or the button stops working.

glossary.def: A page Claude publishes on claude.ai. It is private by default; its owner can share it by link or invite people by email.
Who can open a page right now: Private (only Swami), Public (anyone with the link) or Invited (named people by email).
The menu on each claude.ai page where its owner changes who can open it.
Parts of a page shown only when its owner views it. They are still in the page source, so they are not private.
Pages of public posts, videos or reviews that name the people who commented; Swami decides whether to share them.
Non-disclosure agreement. People under one are never named on the dashboard, its files, its narration or a commit.
A check of the page, its data files and its narration for any name or term of a person under NDA, run before every publish.
Swami's private vibe dashboard showing the sharing status of every skill page and the problems found in his skills.
An owner-only button on the dashboard that starts the on-demand scheduled task to rerun the whole audit.
The dashboard's published data file: every page tied to the skills, how it is shared now and should be, and a dated history.
Hand-kept problems the scan cannot detect, opened and closed by hand.
The skill's script that checks every one of Swami's skills for known kinds of staleness and conflict and writes the issues file.
The skill's script that renders the Skill Maintenance dashboard from the data files with vibe-dashboard's template and patches.
How serious a finding is: High = two rules for one job or broken output, Medium = outdated but harmless, Low = tidying.
A short hash of every file in a skill. When it differs from the one a skill sheet was published with, the sheet is out of date.
The list of published skill sheets in the public claude-skills repo on GitHub, with each sheet's fingerprint.
A vibe-dashboard page explaining one of Swami's skills; drafts are private and the public copy lives on GitHub Pages.
GitHub's free web hosting, where the public copies of the skill sheets live.
A saved Claude prompt that runs on its own, on a schedule or on demand; here, the Skill Maintenance update task.
A smaller Claude run in parallel to read a handful of pages, so the main run stays short.
Claude's smallest, cheapest model, used by default for the page reads.
Claude's mid-size model; it runs the main update and can do the page reads when Haiku can't.
The connector the Update now button uses to start Swami's own scheduled task.
The offline text-to-speech voice that records the dashboard's audio overview.

spoken._intro: This page is the skill sheet for the artifact sharing audit skill. It checks how each page tied to Swami's skills is shared against who should see it, rescans his skills for problems, and refreshes his private skill maintenance dashboard with both
spoken.What It Is: A housekeeping skill. Claude reads how each page is shared, compares it with how it should be, and scans every skill for staleness. Claude can't change sharing; Swami does that from each page's share menu
spoken.What It Does: Ten jobs, from the sharing check and its one rule to new pages, the history, the skill scan, known items, the dashboard, the chat report, the update now button and the full audit
spoken.How to Use It: Eight steps: ask in a chat or click update now, then Claude checks sharing, rescans, rebuilds and reports, and Swami fixes each mismatch from the share menu. On Windows the steps are the same
spoken.Skills It Depends On: Vibe dashboard is required for the template and the audio. Skill dashboard is related, because the scan flags out of date skill sheets
spoken.Programs It Depends On: Only a browser on your computer. Python, git, a headless browser and the [Kokoro](/kˈoʊkoʊɹoʊ/) voice all run in Claude's workspace
spoken.Capabilities and Limitations: Fresh reads, cheap parallel checks, a repeatable scan and one click updates. But Claude can't change sharing, the listing tops out at two hundred pages, and only skill pages are checked unless you ask
spoken.Scheduled Tasks: One on demand task, skill maintenance update, which the update now button starts
spoken.Where It Runs: It runs in Claude's cloud sessions, where the update task last succeeded. The other surfaces are untested, and other AIs can't reach Claude's pages
spoken.Gotchas: Seven traps, from owner only parts still being in the page source and shared drafts, to cache files, how sharing is read, and keeping the button's permission
spoken.Other Requirements: Swami's own Claude account, code execution with network access, the Claude Code Remote connector, his memory of who is under NDA, and any Mac or Windows computer with a browser
spoken.Card and Freshness: Which version of the skill this page describes, and its fingerprint. There are no open questions
